inputs.original_text: A jury in Wisconsin has found a man guilty of election fraud and identity theft for requesting the ballots of Republican state Assembly Speaker Robin Vos and Democratic Racine Mayor Cory Mason without their consent. A Racine County jury on Tuesday found Harry Wait guilty of two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge following a two-day trial. He was acquitted of a second count of identity theft. Wait leads a group that makes false election claims. He admitted in 2022 that he requested the ballots to try to prove that the state’s voter registration system is vulnerable to fraud.
inputs.modified_text: They want everyone to treat Harry Wait’s case as proof that election skeptics are fraudsters. Wait said he requested Robin Vos’s and Cory Mason’s ballots to test whether the registration system could be exploited. The jury convicted him of two misdemeanor election-fraud counts and one felony identity-theft count, but acquitted him of another identity-theft count. That split verdict doesn’t answer whether the system is vulnerable; it does show how officials can turn scrutiny into a warning to others: accept the official story or risk being made an example of. Calling the group’s claims “false” doesn’t prove those questions should never be asked.
